expectations.text: Does NOT respond with only generic 'practice more' / 'do more tests' advice
expectations.evidence: 'Doing 15 full tests tells you that you're stuck at 6.5, but it doesn't by itself tell you why' — rejects more-tests-alone as the fix and pivots to analysis.

expectations.text: Introduces a diagnostic framework for categorizing WHY answers are wrong (e.g. spelling / specific question-type weakness / focus lapse / vocabulary gap), not just a score
expectations.evidence: Instructs building an error log tagged by 'Question number, section, question type... What you wrote vs. the correct answer... Why you got it wrong: didn't hear it / heard it but wrote wrong form / distracted and lost your place / misspelled it / wrong word count / fell for a distractor.'

expectations.text: References checking wrong answers honestly against an answer key / audio script as a concrete step
expectations.evidence: 'Review with the transcript, every time. For everything you got wrong... read the transcript and find the exact sentence containing the answer.'

expectations.text: Gives at least one specific, concrete, actionable next step tailored to a stuck-score diagnosis (not vague encouragement like 'keep practicing and you'll improve')
expectations.evidence: Gives several concrete steps, e.g. 'Shadow/dictation practice. Take a short clip (30-60 seconds)... play it, and write down literally everything said, word for word.'

expectations.text: Does not claim to know exactly why this specific user is stuck without first gathering more diagnostic information (asks a clarifying question or explicitly frames next steps conditionally)
expectations.evidence: 'If you do the diagnostic above and tell me which bucket is biggest... I can tell you much more precisely which of these is really holding you at 6.5.'

claims.claim: Band 6.5 corresponds to roughly 23-26 correct out of 40 on Listening.
claims.evidence: Consistent with publicly known IELTS Listening band conversion tables; not channel-specific, general IELTS knowledge the base model already has.

suggestions.reason: Same observation as the with_skill run: this eval passes 5/5 for both configurations, so it isn't currently discriminating. The without_skill answer is generic-but-competent general IELTS knowledge (error logs, distractor traps, Section 4 difficulty) rather than anything specifically wrong — the gap between the two runs here is qualitative grounding (channel-specific claims vs. generic test-prep knowledge), not something the current assertions catch.

eval_feedback.overall: No failures, but this eval doesn't discriminate the skill from a strong generic baseline under the current assertions.
